name: workflow_update
description:
Replace an existing workflow entirely with a new definition. This is a full replace — every field is overwritten with the new value; there is no patch/merge.

Always call workflow_get first to read the current state before making changes.
The workflow.id inside the JSON must match the id parameter.

Because this is full-replace, preserve unchanged nodes/edges exactly unless the requested change requires editing them. Prefer minimal diffs for workflow fixes: copy the current definition, change only affected node fields, and keep proven working tool-node parameter shapes intact.

The workflow JSON schema is identical to what workflow_create accepts — see that tool's description for the full node type reference, variable reference syntax, and edge routing rules. When editing tool nodes, verify the target tool schema with tool_get and avoid adding optional typed parameters unless required; workflow interpolation/runners may coerce values, so optional numeric/boolean parameters inside tool nodes should be tested or omitted when defaults are acceptable.

id.description: ID of the workflow to update (must already exist)

workflow.description: Complete replacement workflow JSON. All fields are overwritten. Start from workflow_get output and preserve all unrelated nodes/edges/parameters. See workflow_create for workflow schema guidance; call tool_list/tool_get to verify any tool-node action_id values before updating them, and avoid changing proven tool parameter shapes unless necessary.
